ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: the reaction to be balanced given in the image is: ___ MnO4^-(aq) + ___ H+(aq) + ___ C2O4^2-(aq) -> ___ Mn^2+(aq) + ___ H2O(l) + ___ CO2(g). Because H+ appears on the reactant side, this is redox balancing under acidic conditions. Then reason: split the reaction into half-reactions. The reduction half-reaction of manganese is MnO4^- -> Mn^2+, which is balanced under acidic conditions as MnO4^- + 8H+ + 5e^- -> Mn^2+ + 4H2O. The oxidation half-reaction of oxalate is C2O4^2- -> 2CO2 + 2e^-. In order to cancel the electrons, multiply the manganese half-reaction by 2 and the oxalate half-reaction by 5, obtaining the overall reaction: 2MnO4^- + 16H+ + 5C2O4^2- -> 2Mn^2+ + 8H2O + 10CO2. Therefore, the coefficient of MnO4^- is 2.

method.method_draft: First transcribe the reaction from the image and identify it as an acidic redox equation because H+ appears on the reactant side. Split into half-reactions: MnO4^- -> Mn^2+ and C2O4^2- -> CO2. Balance the Mn half-reaction in acid to MnO4^- + 8H+ + 5e^- -> Mn^2+ + 4H2O. Balance oxalate oxidation as C2O4^2- -> 2CO2 + 2e^-. Multiply the Mn half-reaction by 2 and the oxalate half-reaction by 5 to cancel 10 electrons, then combine. Read off the MnO4^- coefficient as 2.
